doc.title: Steve Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 15, 2017

title: Naming his composition 'Abena's Gaze'
summary: Rowe scats a melody Davis recognises as his tune 'Abena's Gaze', written for his wife.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You have some good answers. Do you know that? Okay you’re a composer too.
And I’m going to make an attempt here, see if you can name this tune. Starts on beat 4. Oh by the way the sound, that’s one of our trombone players here. I’ve lined up a lesson.
Okay here we go. Starts on beat 4.
Is that the melody? © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
I believe so. I’m not sure I have the pitches right. I wrote the rhythm down.
Oh “Abena’s Gaze.” [scats] Where did it go? [scats] Yeah. That’s it. “Abena’s Gaze.”
I like that. It’s hooky and, where did it come from?
